elements.element: No minimum purchase, spend, or volume commitment applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly requires Customer to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 during the current twelve-month term. Section 12.3's contrary acknowledgement creates ambiguity but does not eliminate the express commitment unambiguously.

elements.element: Customer owes fees only for actual usage or Services it affirmatively orders.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 requires a true-up for any commitment shortfall, which may require payment for Services neither used nor ordered. Section 9.4 limits fees after convenience termination but does not cure the general shortfall obligation.

elements.element: Any commitment applies only to the current term and does not continue into later terms.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 limits the commitment to the current term 'only.'

elements.element: The current committed term has a duration of twelve months.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly identifies the current term as a 'twelve-month term.'
Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer may reduce the commitment.

elements.element: Customer may effect a reduction on thirty days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 permits reduction 'on thirty days' notice.'

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall is settled through a true-up.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly provides that 'any shortfall is settled by a true-up.'

elements.element: No penalty is imposed for a commitment shortfall.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly specifies a true-up 'rather than a penalty.'

result.reason: The operative redline reaches every fallback element but not the preferred position. It is narrowly directed to the minimum commitment. However, the resulting agreement is internally inconsistent: §12.3 says Customer made no minimum-volume commitment, while §2.1 imposes one, and §9.4 says Customer owes fees only for conforming Services through termination, which may conflict with a shortfall true-up. Those conflicts materially impair coherence despite the margin comment identifying them.
